Miller and colleagues evaluated MegaDetector 5A on 1,485,924 time-lapse images from 42 cameras at three South Florida sites. At a detection threshold of 0.05, 88,863 images remained for human review, a reported 94.0% reduction. Manual review took 265 hours. Computer processing took 27.7 hours, and the authors estimated a 43.5-hour hybrid workflow by adding human review time calculated from the manual review rate. About 16 hours of that total represent estimated human review, not separately timed hybrid labor. MegaDetector located animals; people assigned snake species in Timelapse2. The hybrid method found 217 independent snake events, compared with 378 manually and 447 across both methods. Snake-image recall was 17.1% for the hybrid method and 96.2% manually. Results differed by species: the hybrid method found five of six Burmese-python events and more North American racer events than manual review. Neither method found every event. The study documents reduced review work with detection losses. It does not document a management decision, population improvement, or net financial saving.

The user already held a genetic result (homozygous A1298C MTHFR from a Function Health panel), five PDFs of laboratory results and a written symptom timeline. They gave all of it to the model rather than a description of symptoms alone. A paid reasoning model (o3, by the user's account) was asked to reconcile B12 values in the laboratory's normal range with persistent neurological symptoms. The mutation was not found by ChatGPT. The user wrote that a Function Health panel showed the homozygous A1298C MTHFR variant. The AppSo account says the same (“在功能医学检查中发现”). What ChatGPT (o3, per the user) added was the inference. Given about five paragraphs of history and five PDFs of results, it concluded the symptoms were “on par with the mutation”. It concluded that B12 values that looked normal on paper might not be utilized, so supplementation was warranted. The doctor confirmed the reading and the supplement. The user then improved. The counterfactual is unproven. The same results were available to the doctor. The user had earlier been told the symptoms were anxiety and given an SSRI and Xanax. Whether the improvement came from the supplement, from regression, or from expectation is unknown. Livemint (“The AI flagged a possible genetic mutation”) and the Monitor's summary (“identification of genetic mutations missed by doctors”) overstate the model's role. The ACMG guideline and the ifeng piece also put the MTHFR premise itself in doubt.
